title: Choose the visual world — Kiki's Mandarin sentence builder
question: The roll assigned 印谱 · The Seal Album. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: 印谱 · The Seal Album
options.lineage: 篆刻 seal carving and the 印谱 impression album: pages of vermilion stamps in strict grids with tiny black annotations
options.thesis: Every chunk of Chinese is a carved stone face, and building a sentence stamps it onto the page — so the builder refuses the neutral spreadsheet every sentence-builder tool ships.
materials: 阴刻 / 阳刻 inverse states
options.viewport: A dense 印谱 page: the builder's columns as ruled cells of stone-faced chunks, the sentence line beneath as a row of wet vermilion impressions, empty slots drawn as blind-embossed ghost frames, hanzi at poster scale with pinyin pinned to each character.
options.risk: Vermilion-on-pale can drift into the cream-paper-and-red-accent look every model ships; it only holds if the red commits as whole fields and the ground stays cool stone, never warm cream.

raised.raise: Absence is drawn as deliberately as presence: an unfilled sentence slot is a blind-embossed 界格 ghost frame, never an invisible gap.
No generic button shells anywhere — the carved seal face is the control, and activity navigation is set in type.
Vermilion commits as flat unmodulated fields owning whole regions, not as an accent sprinkled over neutral.
Difficulty is one governing axis; moving it recolours and re-ranks the whole vocabulary panel in step.
Pinyin and gloss are annotations pinned to the chunk they describe, and any generated sentence can be traced back to its exact path through the table.

options.label: 田字格 · The Copybook
options.lineage: 字帖 character-practice paper: red squares with faint crossed guides, model characters in red, tracing ghosts in grey
options.thesis: The single sheet every Chinese learner on earth has written on, turned into the whole interface.
options.viewport: The builder laid out on ruled practice paper, each chunk sitting in its own red 田字格 cell with crossed guides showing through the hanzi.
options.risk: It is the most obvious answer for a Chinese-learning product and the one most runs would land on, and as a whole-app world it is thin: grid paper plus red ink, with warm-cream drift built in.

options.label: Interactive Type Specimen
options.lineage: variable-font specimen pages: one giant glyph, an axis slider, a breathing glyph grid, live coordinate readout
options.thesis: The builder as a specimen of the language: one enormous character, tiny mono labels, and one slider that remaps the whole page.
options.viewport: One hanzi at enormous scale over a glyph grid of every character in the builder, with a reading-level axis and a monospace readout of level, character count and known-vocabulary percentage.
options.case: Fuses well on product clarity — hanzi genuinely wants poster scale and a live axis is exactly what a differentiated reading level is — but a teacher does not identify with a type foundry, so it holds one axis only.
options.risk: Reads as a designer's toy rather than a classroom tool, and near-white plus one orange accent is itself a saturated pattern.

options.label: 麻将牌 · Tile Rack
options.lineage: bone-and-bamboo mahjong tiles on green felt, engraved and painted characters, tiles racked and rearranged
options.thesis: Chunks are tiles you rack and rearrange; a finished sentence is a winning hand.
options.viewport: A rack of tiles across the foot of the screen, the builder's columns above as suits, tiles sliding into a sentence hand with a genuine clack.
options.case: Strong audience identification for Chinese game play and it maps cleanly onto click-to-build activities, but a tile rack cannot hold the dense authoring table a teacher needs, so it loses product clarity.
options.risk: Skins a serious classroom tool as a gambling parlour, which some schools will reject outright.

options.label: Seven-Segment Display
options.lineage: bedside clocks, price totems, scoreboards — one eight-cell mask where unlit segments are designed too
options.thesis: The interface as a rigid cell mask where only which segments light ever changes.
options.viewport: Fixed digit slots on near-black, values slamming between states with nothing sliding.
options.case: Hanzi cannot be drawn on an eight-cell mask, so the fusion destroys the product's only content; and a Mandarin classroom has no relationship to scoreboards.
options.kept: Absence designed as deliberately as light.
options.risk: Illegible for the writing system the product exists to teach.

options.label: Metro Typographic Tiles
options.lineage: flat tiles, giant cropped lowercase, colour fields as content, chrome deleted
options.thesis: Delete the chrome; the type itself is the interface.
options.viewport: A wide panorama of square tiles on pure black, headlines cropped off the right edge.
options.case: Cropping display type off the canvas is fatal when the display type is hanzi a learner is decoding, and black-plus-cyan fights sustained character reading.
options.kept: Chrome deleted: no button shells, type is the control.
options.risk: Dated Windows-Phone canon with no link to the audience's world.

options.label: Zoo & Gardens Guide Map
options.lineage: a creased visitor guide map of swelling flat-colour lobes divided by coastline
options.thesis: Every area is a lobe of flat colour and the coastline does all the dividing.
options.viewport: One green lobe swelling past two frame edges, a yellow capsule pinned to its coast.
options.case: School-adjacent and childlike in the right way, but the sentence builder is an irreducibly strict grid; organic lobes would wreck the scanability the authoring table depends on.
options.kept: Flat colour committing at page scale as content, not accent.
options.risk: Reads as a primary-school wall display for a secondary-school tool.

options.label: Mesophotic Deep Dive
options.lineage: a technical descent down a volcanic island wall, dive-computer digits, marine snow
options.thesis: One vertical depth axis governs light, colour, content and obligation together.
options.viewport: A vertical dive profile with observations pinned to their exact depth as the light drains.
options.case: A scuba metaphor over Mandarin grammar is arbitrary — nothing in a teacher's or student's world connects — and the staged darkening actively harms sustained reading.
options.kept: One governing axis that changes colour, content and state in step.
options.risk: Atmosphere with no product truth underneath it.

options.label: Tensegrity Breathing Column
options.lineage: carbon rods and red cord held apart by opposing forces, annotations pinned to nodes on leader lines
options.thesis: Trace any load to its counterforce; layout obeys the strut network, not a page grid.
options.viewport: A floating column of rods with force values on leader lines, layout following the network.
options.case: The traceability idea is real, but an engineering-studio world has no purchase on a language classroom, and a layout that obeys a force network cannot host the authoring table.
options.kept: Annotations pinned to the node they describe, every relationship traceable.
options.risk: Engineering cosplay over a humanities tool.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What a language-practice web app ships: white cards, a blue primary button, rounded chips, a friendly mascot.
canonCard.viewport: A centred hero headline over a screenshot, feature cards in threes, a blue Get started button.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from Quizlet, Duolingo clones and every other language tool, by design.
